Article Title: ‘Gyanesh Kumar must be removed’: DMK demands CEC’s ouster, backs student protests
Article Text:
DMK passes resolution demanding CEC's ouster, backs student protests

DMK recalls opposition to SIR

Party backs student protests

DMK targets Congress, TVK over SIR stance

DMK MPs to petition President for electoral reforms

NEW DELHI: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an inquiry into his conduct, accusing him of overseeing the systematic disenfranchisement of legitimate voters through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The party also extended its support to student protests against the exercise and resolved to seek the scrapping of the SIR and a return to paper ballots.The resolutions were adopted at a meeting of the DMK Parliamentary Party, chaired by party president and former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin at the party headquarters, Anna Arivalayam, in Chennai.The meeting adopted four resolutions, including one demanding Kumar’s removal, another extending solidarity to student organisations protesting against the SIR, and a third accusing the Congress and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) of maintaining double standards on the issue.The DMK's demand comes amid a wider political campaign against Kumar, with opposition groups calling for his resignation and announcing a Tiranga march.News agency ANI reported citing resolution that Stalin had opposed the SIR in July 2025 after reports emerged of large-scale voter deletions in Bihar, the first state where the exercise was introduced. He also participated in the Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar, accompanied by DMK deputy general secretary and parliamentary party leader Kanimozhi Karunanidhi.The party said Stalin subsequently raised concerns after the Election Commission announced on October 27, 2025, that the SIR would be conducted in 12 states, including Tamil Nadu. He alleged that the BJP was seeking to extend the exercise to Tamil Nadu as part of a conspiracy to disenfranchise voters.The DMK also objected to conducting the revision during November and December, citing the monsoon and festive seasons. Its MPs, the resolution said, had repeatedly raised concerns in Parliament over the exercise and its potential impact on eligible voters.Referring to the 2025 Bihar Assembly election results, the party recalled Stalin's November 15 remarks on problems within the opposition alliance, including disagreements over seat-sharing and candidates from alliance partners contesting against one another. However, Stalin had maintained that these political difficulties did not justify alleged lapses by the Election Commission.The resolution said public confidence in the poll body had fallen to an unprecedented low.In a separate resolution, the DMK extended full solidarity to student organisations protesting against the SIR and reiterated its demand for Kumar's removal.The party said Stalin was among the first leaders in Tamil Nadu to condemn the exercise and accused the CEC of disregarding the Constitution, acting unilaterally and exceeding his authority. Stalin also reiterated his criticism during by-election campaigns in Dharapuram and Madurantakam, the resolution said.The party maintained that its position remained unchanged: the SIR should be scrapped and Kumar removed from office. It also pledged support to protests organised by democratic groups seeking these demands.In its third resolution, the DMK accused the Congress and TVK of double standards over the electoral revision.The resolution criticised the Congress for opposing the SIR at the national level while, according to the DMK, remaining reluctant to raise similar concerns in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. It argued that allegations of irregularities should be addressed consistently across states.The party also questioned the TVK's position, asking why its leader, actor Vijay, had not publicly opposed the SIR or demanded Kumar's removal despite democratic groups sharing a platform with the party during protests.The DMK further alleged that certain individuals associated with the Congress were praising the TVK for personal benefits. It accused both parties of misleading the public and warned against attempts to provoke a political confrontation with the DMK, which is not part of their alliance.Under its fourth resolution, the DMK decided that its MPs would submit a formal petition to the President of India seeking electoral reforms under Stalin's guidance.The party's demands include the complete scrapping of the SIR and the use of pre-SIR electoral rolls for all upcoming elections. It also called for discontinuing electronic voting machines and restoring the traditional paper ballot system, arguing that the move would help rebuild public confidence in the electoral process.(With inputs from ANI)
Article Summary: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) demands immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The party also extended its support to student protests against the exercise and resolved to seek the scrapping of the SIR and a return to paper ballots.

Article Title: Behind the lights and grandeur: What it takes and costs to build a Durga Pujo pandal
Article Text:
​Before the dhak begins: The money and machinery behind a Durga pujo​

The quiet work before the dhak

The budget

The pandal takes the biggest share

The idol costs a fifth

A theme, decided half a year early

Two months, or more

Six months, one theme, lakhs of rupees

Where the money comes from

The people who are paid

What it costs to raise a Durga Pujo

What the numbers leave out

Everything, from beginning to end

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the cost of a medium-scale Durga Puja should be capped to keep it accessible? Yes, absolutely! No, let it vary based on demand. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Long before the first beat of the dhak, a Durga Pujo has already been decided, priced and partly built. The goddess arrives in autumn, but the people who bring her to a neighbourhood start months earlier, with a theme, a budget and a list of permissions that must be collected one office at a time.To the crowds who walk through a pandal's gates, a pujo is a few days of colour, light and sound. To the club that puts it up, it is a yearly project that runs on money raised from the neighbourhood, a small circle of skilled craftsmen and a large number of people who all have to be in the right place on the right day. In West Bengal that project is repeated in locality after locality, each with its own ledger.The ledger is not small. A medium-scale pujo costs several lakh rupees, and the biggest share does not go to the idol at the centre of it all. It goes to the structure built around her. Most visitors never see the figures, the deadlines or the people behind them, and that is exactly how the organisers want it. A pujo is meant to arrive as a finished thing.Nirmal, a pujo organiser from West Bengal who has run one for the past 10 years, knows that ledger well. "A medium scale pujo in West Bengal would cost somewhere between 10 to 15 lakhs," he says. "Every year the budget increases as per the market inflation."That second sentence matters as much as the first. A committee that spent a certain amount last year should expect to spend more this year on the same pujo, before it adds a single new ambition. For a club working with money collected from its neighbours, the target keeps moving upward, and the neighbours are asked to keep up with it.Ask him what costs the most and the answer is immediate. "The pandal costs the most," he says. Not the lighting, not the idol, not the food. He puts the pandal at around Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh for a medium-scale pujo, which makes it the line the rest of the budget has to work around.Next to the pandal, the idol is a modest line. "Whatever the pandal costs, the idol costs its one-fifth," Nirmal says. For a medium-scale pujo, that works out to around Rs 80,000.It is a striking ratio. The figure at the heart of the festival, the one every visitor has come to see, costs a fraction of the structure that shelters her.Within the idol's cost, the most expensive element is gold. Certain gold items are designated for it, among them an ornament that is given by the club organising the pujo. The ornament comes from the organisers themselves, which makes it a different kind of expense from the rest.A pandal needs a theme, and the theme needs time. "The theme is decided at least six months ago," Nirmal says, meaning at least six months before the pujo. That is a long lead for a festival that lasts only days.Who decides it varies. In some committees, he says, there is a specific person whose sole job is deciding the theme. In others, the pandal makers can decide it too. The choice matters for more than looks, because the budget is also decided through the theme. Once the idea is fixed, the cost of building it can be worked out, and the money follows.This is why the calendar starts so early. A theme chosen six months out leaves room to price the work, find the right artisan and settle the budget before construction begins. By the time the neighbourhood sees the first bamboo go up, the important decisions have already been made.Construction is where the calendar turns uncertain. Asked how long a medium-scale pandal takes to build, Nirmal is candid. "It depends on the workers, to be honest," he says. "Some can build the same pandal in two months, whereas some will require more time."The reason, as he describes it, is a shortage of skill. "The skilled pandal makers are not a lot in number. Mostly there is just one skilled artisan and a lot of people work under him."That structure explains a good deal. The quality of the pandal and the speed at which it rises rest heavily on one person, with a large crew following his lead. For an organiser, choosing a pandal maker is therefore as much a scheduling decision as a financial one. A maker who is slow, or one who is booked elsewhere, can put the whole timeline at risk.The funding model is local. "Every area or colony has a designated club which builds a pandal," Nirmal explains. "And then they get chanda, donations, advertisements that ultimately make the pujo what it is."There is also help from the state. This year, he says, the West Bengal government is providing Rs 1 lakh to small-scale pujos, and electricity is completely free. Free power removes a bill that would otherwise sit beside the lighting and the pandal. The Rs 1 lakh grant, though, is meant for small-scale pujos. Set against a medium-scale budget of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh, most of the money still has to come from the neighbourhood, from donors and from advertisers.Some costs are smaller but just as fixed. The priest's expenditure, Nirmal says, is around Rs 30,000 to Rs 40,000. The dhaki, whose drumming is as much a part of the pujo as the idol, is paid around Rs 10,000. On top of that, he gets free food, lodging and clothes.Those extras are part of the arrangement. A dhaki who is housed and fed for the duration of the pujo is a cost the committee carries beyond the headline fee. Nirmal was also asked about bhog expenditure, but his answer covered only the priest and the dhaki.Add up the lines Nirmal named, the pandal, the idol, the priest and the dhaki, and the total lands somewhere between roughly Rs 4.2 lakh and Rs 6.3 lakh. His estimate for the whole pujo is Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh.The gap is considerable. It covers everything else a pujo needs, including the lighting and food he named only to rule them out as the biggest expense. Nirmal did not break down how that money is divided.Asked about the biggest challenge organisers face, Nirmal does not name a single expense. "The biggest challenge is that everything from the beginning to the end is completed properly," he says.That includes permissions. "You have to get proper permissions like the police and the fire department," he says, "and it takes a lot of people to complete a pujo and to make a pujo what it is."The pandal maker and his crew, the artisan working on the idol, the priest, the dhaki and the club members collecting funds are all working towards the same date. Seen this way, the Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh is only part of what a pujo demands. The rest is coordination, and much of Nirmal's decade in the job has gone into it.For the people who walk through the gates, the pujo arrives as a finished thing. For the club behind it, it began at least six months earlier with a decision about a theme, and it will begin again next year at a higher cost.

Article Title: 'Internet access is fundamental right': SC suggests ‘child mode’ for social media accounts
Article Text:
Blanket restrictions are not the answer

Building on earlier rulings

Poll Vote & Share your view Should social media platforms implement a child mode to enhance online safety for children? Yes, it is necessary No, it's not effective 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Saturday declared access to and use of the internet a fundamental right for every individual, including children, under Articles 21 and 19(1)(a) of the Constitution, observing that “The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. ”The bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran also suggested that children’s online safety should be strengthened through measures such as a ‘child mode’ for social media accounts, rather than denying them access to the internet altogether, LiveLaw reported.A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran made the observations while issuing directions to strengthen mechanisms for detecting and removing child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) from social media platforms and other online services.According to LiveLaw, the bench said: "..we have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing.The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. Our children are entitled to both."The bench acknowledged that the internet, in its present form, poses safety risks to children. However, it said restricting children's access because online platforms had failed to detect and remove harmful material would amount to mistaking the victim for the problem.The court examined whether children should be completely shielded from the internet and social media in the interest of their safety. It noted that the right to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) includes the right to know, receive and impart information and ideas.Describing the internet as a marketplace of ideas, creative expression and information, the court said its value extended beyond the material available online to the opportunities it provided for learning, communication and access to information."For many children, particularly in remote areas, it is often the only source of learning and information," the court observed.It also noted that the internet could be particularly important for children with special needs, for whom online platforms might be the only place to find companionship with others facing similar circumstances.The bench referred to the Supreme Court's 2020 judgment in Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, which held that "the freedom of speech and expression and the freedom to carry on any trade or business through the medium of the internet is constitutionally protected as a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution."In that judgment, the court had refrained from expressing a view on whether the right to access the internet, by itself, constituted a fundamental right.The bench also referred to the 2025 judgment in Pragya Prasun & Ors. v. Union of India, in which the court recognised the right to digital access as a fundamental right under Article 21.
Article Summary: Supreme Court declares access to and use of the internet a fundamental right for every individual, including children. “The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. ” bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran said.

Article Title: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee faces court warrants over 2018 video targeting BJP IT cell
Article Text:
Bailable warrants issued against Dhruv Rathee in defamation case linked to 2018 video

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has issued bailable warrants against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case, news agency PTI reported.The case stems from a video published by Rathee in May 2018, in which he allegedly claimed that the Bharatiya Janata Party’s ( BJP ) Information Technology cell had attempted to bribe a man to defame him. The video was posted on Rathee’s social media account and later retweeted by Arvind Kejriwal, who was then the Delhi chief minister.The complainant, Vikas Sankrityayan, also known as Vikas Pandey, subsequently initiated defamation proceedings against Rathee and Kejriwal over the video and its circulation.Earlier, on October 12, Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain of the Saket court ordered fresh summons to Rathee after the complainant submitted that repeated attempts to serve him had remained unsuccessful since the proceedings began.The complainant’s counsel, advocate Samaksh Sharma, told the court that the summons had remained unserved for several years as Rathee primarily lived abroad. The court was informed, however, that Rathee was then in India and residing at an address in Gurugram, Haryana.The magistrate noted that Rathee had first been summoned on July 23, 2019, and that the complainant had continued to pursue service of the summons.The court allowed Pandey to accompany the process server and directed him to deposit the process fee within two days. The next hearing was scheduled for October 17, 2026.Separately, Rathee is facing a defamation suit before the Saket court over a video that allegedly claimed Lord Ram and Goddess Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile.The complainants, who identified themselves as Hindu devotees, alleged that the video hurt their religious sentiments. They have also sought an ex-parte ad-interim injunction restraining Google from restoring, hosting, uploading, sharing or disseminating the video, or any video with identical or similar content, after notice and verification of the URL, during the pendency of the suit.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has issued bailable warrants against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee. The case stems from a video published by Rathee in May 2018. The video was posted on Rathee's social media account and later retweeted by Arvind Kejriwal.

Article Title: ‘He spoke to Putin to buy diesel’: Ex-diplomat Fabian after Trump waives sanctions over Russian oil
Article Text:
"President Trump contradicts President Trump... what he says today is not what he might say tomorrow": Ex-diplomat Fabian

Trump pauses sanctions

What it means for India

NEW DELHI: Former diplomat KP Fabian on Saturday questioned the rationale behind the US tariff pressure on India over Russian oil purchases, arguing that Washington’s own decision to waive sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act exposed a contradiction in its approach.His remarks came after US President Donald Trump earlier today waived sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.Speaking to ANI, Fabian said, “Trump himself spoke to Putin to buy diesel. If America itself is buying, either it should sanction itself, which is ridiculous."He also argued that the tariff threats against India were a negotiating tactic aimed at securing a favourable trade deal rather than a genuine response to New Delhi’s energy purchases from Russia.“Certain tariffs were imposed, and the court in the United States said that Trump had no business."Fabian said Trump had avoided directly confronting Chinese President Xi Jinping over Russian oil purchases because China was a major buyer of Russian exports and Washington wanted closer engagement with Beijing.“Contrary to the Lindsey Graham Act, President Trump did not dare to mention it to Xi Jinping because China is a top buyer, 50 per cent of Russia’s exports.India comes next at 37 per cent,” he told ANI.However, Trump earlier on Saturday paused provisions of the Graham Act that could have imposed tariffs of up to 100% on goods imported into the US from the five largest buyers of Russian crude oil or natural gas, including India and China.The move comes against the backdrop of rising diesel prices in the US ahead of the November midterm elections and a reported agreement under which Russia would supply diesel fuel to Washington.Trump invoked Section 115 of the Act, which authorises the US president to waive certain sanctions-related provisions and restrictions involving foreign entities.“I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification, consistent with section 115(b) of the Graham Act,” Trump said in the order.Russia continues to be the single largest supplier of oil for India. A waiver of tariffs of up to 100% which may have come into place in the coming days means that India can continue importing oil in large numbers from Moscow without any economic fallout.If 100% tariffs had been imposed by the Trump administration, then it would have hit exporters as the US is the largest trading partner for India. At the same time, any sanctions may have rendered Russian crude economically unviable which would have added to the supply crunch at a time when Middle East tensions continue.
Article Summary: Former diplomat KP Fabian questioned the rationale behind the US tariff pressure on India over Russian oil purchases. He argued that Washington’s own decision to waive sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act exposed a contradiction in its approach. Fabian said the tariff threats against India were a negotiating tactic aimed at securing a favourable trade deal.

Article Title: Indian woman jailed over son’s fatal stabbing faces possible deportation from UK
Article Text:
Vickrum Digwa's mother Kiran Kaur was jailed for three years in July for assisting an offender

Kirpan argument sparks controversy

Police conduct under investigation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

An Indian woman jailed for helping her son after he fatally stabbed an 18-year-old student in Southampton could face deportation to India following her early release from prison, British authorities have indicated.According to new agency PTI, the UK Home Office said it would seek to deport foreign criminals at the earliest opportunity, although it did not refer specifically to Kiran Kaur, 53. Foreign nationals sentenced to at least 12 months in prison are generally considered for deportation, subject to exceptions and legal challenges.Kaur was sentenced to three years in prison in July for assisting an offender by removing the weapon used by her son, Vickrum Digwa, to kill Henry Nowak on December 3, 2025. She is expected to be released early under a government scheme aimed at reducing overcrowding in British prisons.Digwa, 23, was sentenced to life imprisonment in June, with a minimum term of 21 years before he becomes eligible for parole.Both Kaur and her son have been granted permission to challenge their sentences, with their appeals scheduled to be heard by the UK Court of Appeal on November 5.The case drew widespread attention after Digwa sought to invoke a religious self-defence argument involving the kirpan, a ceremonial knife that Sikhs are legally permitted to carry in the UK.During Kaur’s sentencing, Justice William Mousley stressed that the kirpan was a symbol of religious faith and was not intended to be carried for offensive purposes. He said any use of the weapon in self-defence would have to be justified by circumstances involving great seriousness and urgency.The judge also criticised Kaur for removing the weapon rather than challenging her son’s actions and encouraging him to do the right thing.He acknowledged that she had experienced a difficult life in India before marrying and moving to the UK nearly 30 years ago. He said she had acted to protect her son rather than for personal gain and was unlikely to reoffend, while making clear that her actions warranted punishment.British Sikh organisations and parliamentarians subsequently condemned what they described as the misrepresentation of the kirpan, stressing that religious protection did not justify the violence in this case.The killing also triggered scrutiny of police conduct after body-worn camera footage showed officers handcuffing Nowak following Digwa’s allegations that he had been subjected to racism. Those allegations were subsequently rejected in court.The Independent Office for Police Conduct is investigating the officers’ handling of the incident amid allegations of “two-tier” policing, referring to claims that different communities were treated unequally.The case has heightened tensions in Southampton and the wider Hampshire and Isle of Wight area.Kaur’s potential deportation remains subject to the applicable immigration process, while the outcome of the appeals against her sentence and Digwa’s life term is awaited.
Article Summary: Kiran Kaur, 53, was jailed for three years in July for assisting an offender. She removed the weapon used by her son, Vickrum Digwa, to kill Henry Nowak. Home Office said it would seek to deport foreign criminals at the earliest opportunity.

Article Title: ‘Foreign-inspired terrorism no longer visible’: Home Secy Govind Mohan on changing internal security landscape
Article Text:
Home Secy Govind Mohan speaks on changing internal security landscape

NEW DELHI: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan has said that foreign-inspired terrorism has been largely contained in India, barring a few areas, while homegrown terrorism has nearly been eliminated."Homegrown terrorism has almost ended, while foreign-inspired terrorism is no longer visible in any other part of the country," he said.Speaking in Hyderabad, Mohan also identified narcotics, cybercrime and illegal immigration as key challenges facing Indian Police Service (IPS) trainees."Militant naxalism has come to an end; North East insurgency reduced to minuscule levels," he said.His remarks come amid a push by the Centre for stronger regional cooperation to combat terrorism and organised crime.Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Tuesday called on BIMSTEC member countries to strengthen cooperation against terrorism, disrupt terrorist financing and prevent terrorist networks from establishing safe havens in the region.Addressing the first Home Ministers’ Meeting of BIMSTEC countries in New Delhi, Shah said India follows a policy of “zero tolerance” towards terrorism and stressed the need for collective action to strengthen regional security.“Hosting the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting is a matter of great pride and fortune for India. BIMSTEC, in a way, has become an essential platform for regional integration, economic cooperation and collective security.With the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India is going ahead today," Shah said.“We have always been committed to peace, coexistence and human welfare. We continue to be committed to these even today. India has never believed in attacking any country or establishing dominance over them. India has always believed in upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of every country and peaceful resolution of differences,” he added.Shah said trust among BIMSTEC members was strengthened by the understanding that each country's security arrangements should contribute to the security of others.He called for a collective commitment to ensure that terrorist networks could not find shelter, establish bases or training facilities, mobilise resources or carry out activities against other member countries.
Article Summary: Militant naxalism has come to an end; North East insurgency reduced to minuscule levels. Home Minister Amit Shah on Tuesday called on BIMSTEC member countries to strengthen cooperation against terrorism, disrupt terrorist financing and prevent terrorist networks from establishing safe havens in the region.

Article Title: Middle East conflict: India pushes for 'resolution through dialogue and diplomacy' at UNSC
Article Text:
Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region

India flags attacks on commercial ships

Calls for de-escalation, protection of maritime routes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, on Friday condemned attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East, warning that the escalating hostilities pose a serious threat to regional stability and the safety of Indian nationals.Speaking at the UN Security Council ’s open debate on the Middle East, Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region, highlighting that around 10 million Indians live in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and contribute to their economies.He called for restraint and de-escalation, expressing concern over attacks on civilian infrastructure that have resulted in casualties, including the death of Indian citizen Mohammed Yusuf Ali in Riyadh.Harish said India stood in complete solidarity with the government and people of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty following the recent attacks.He also raised concerns over attacks on commercial shipping, including the India-flagged MV DP World Kaveri earlier this week and MT Petro Dolphin and MT Walthera last week.“All attacks on commercial shipping and merchant mariners are legally and morally indefensible,” he said, adding that several of the affected vessels had Indian seafarers whose safety and security remained India's direct responsibility.India reiterated the need for an immediate de-escalation of hostilities and a resolution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.Harish said attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure must cease, stressing that freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways must be upheld in accordance with international law.He further added that focus on maritime security must not divert attention from the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. It condemned the October 7, 2023 attacks and reiterated its support for a negotiated two-state solution, the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2803, and continued development and humanitarian assistance.v
Article Summary: India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, on Friday condemned attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East. Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region.

Article Title: If every citizen becomes a journalist, it will create problems for all, says SC
Article Text:
"Will require a detailed examination whether the right to freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist" the court said.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it will be problematic if every citizen becomes a journalist as PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues already teeming with hordes of accredited reporters from registered media houses.Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists covering the protests and insisted on Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation. She said there must be a national protocol for police not to obstruct the professional work of any journalist who has an identity card from the employer.CJI Kant, however, struck a note of caution. “We must also keep one thing in mind. If everyone starts becoming a journalist, it will create problems for every other person,” he said. Justice Bagchi said, “It will require a detailed examination whether the right to freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist. That is difficult. There are layers of protection for accredited journalists, those employed in registered media houses or whether they are freelance journalists, influencers or reel-makers.CJI Kant said, “The issue requires detailed examination — whether there should be a certain category of journalists to whom extra level of protection should be given.” Justice Bagchi added, “The Working Journalists Act makes classes among journalists. We must examine all that.”Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said in the present era of digital technology, any person with a mobile phone could claim to be an independent or freelance journalist when he/she would, in fact, be only making reels to garner popularity on social media to earn money by either presenting one-sided stories or sensationalising incidents.Mehta supported the contention that women journalists should not be harrassed, but argued that the same consideration should be extended to women police personnel as well.
Article Summary: PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues. Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists.

Article Title: SIR protests: Opposition has found common ground. But can it stay united?
Article Text:
Members of INDIA bloc at high-tea hosted at Rahul Gandhi's residence in Delhi (File photo)

Delhi Police detained more than 3,000 people attempting to reach Jantar Mantar for the protest.

What Rahul Gandhi said after CJP leaders were arrested.

Opposition closes ranks

From Mamata to Kejriwal, opposition leaders back arrested CJP leaders

The counter

Has the opposition finally found its feet?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: "All protests are one," Congress leader Rahul Gandhi declared on Wednesday as opposition parties rallied behind two Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders sent to judicial custody following demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke welcomed Rahul's support, thanking the Congress leader for standing with the arrested protesters.Just days ago, that was hardly how things looked on Delhi's streets, where Congress and CJP appeared to be competing for space and prominence while leading separate campaigns against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Congress-led INDIA bloc was organising its own demonstrations, while CJP, which had mobilised thousands of protesters in July, prepared separately for Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10.AAP, TMC and the Left were willing to join CJP's agitation, but Congress kept its distance. Their objective was the same, but they were fighting for it separately. Many wondered why.On October 10, the Delhi police enforced an unprecedented clampdown in the national capital to prevent mobilisation for CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0. Thousands of protesters were dragged on the streets and detained.Such was the intensity of police action that the CJP stir could not even take off.The top CJP leaders were arrested from a plane on landing in Delhi, drawing flak from some quarters for their easy “surrender.” Several political parties stood with the cockroaches, but the Congress stayed away.The trigger for greater unity came after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested on October 14 following their attempt to protest at Jantar Mantar by waving the Tricolour. Rahul Gandhi came out in open support for first time, and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke thanked him.The dynamics now seem to be changing, with Congress and CJP more willing to support each other, if not formally join forces. But why? Have both sides realised the limitations of organising separate protests for the same cause? Let's decode this shift.In June, when CJP protested against the NEET paper leak and demanded the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, Congress stayed away. Rahul was leading his own programme, Chhatron Ki Goonj, on similar issues.AAP, the Left and social activists joined CJP at Jantar Mantar. The movement gained momentum with Sonam Wangchuk and AISA leader Neha Bora sitting on an indefinite fast. But Congress continued to stay away.On July 20, Delhi Police launched a major operation against students and young protesters who had reached the capital on CJP's call. The next day, Rahul joined the agitation and staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, shifting Congress's focus from its own campaign.However, with the government entering negotiations with CJP and later accepting its demands, including Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, Congress was left on the sidelines.The anti-paper leak protests were perhaps a wake-up call for political parties, especially Congress, as large numbers of young people mobilised behind CJP. Prime Minister Modi subsequently turned to Instagram to reach out to Gen Z, while other parties were left to rethink their youth outreach.Congress had been at the forefront of the 'vote chori' campaign, with Rahul holding press conferences highlighting alleged discrepancies in electoral rolls. The party also led a yatra in Bihar ahead assembly elections in the state.The momentum gradually faded, before an Indian Express report on differences within the Election Commission over SIR returned the issue to centre stage. CJP took up the issue, organising a Mumbai rally and setting an October 10 deadline for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, failing which it called for Jantar Mantar 2.0.Congress and the INDIA bloc also stepped up their campaign, announcing a six-point action plan that included an October 6 street protest. With CJP's mobilisation approaching, INDIA bloc leaders returned to the streets for four consecutive days until October 9, perhaps keen not to be left on the sidelines again. But on October 10, the D-day of CJP mobilisation, Rahul was in Chennai and the Congress stayed away.Another change had taken place between July and October. Civil society groups and activists associated with CJP's earlier movement were now actively participating in the INDIA bloc's SIR campaign.The most prominent was Neha Bora, national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA). During the October 12 march towards the Supreme Court, Rahul walked with his hands on the shoulders of Bora and Priyanka Gandhi, with senior opposition leaders following behind.The moment appeared to signal Congress's willingness to bring prominent youth protest faces into its campaign. Political analyst Uday Chandra explained the significance of this shift."Congress under RG recognises that youth-led protests have mobilised ordinary people beyond the reach of traditional party organisations. Neha Bora is an interesting bridge between these worlds, though she leads AISA, a Left student organisation, not CJP," Chandra said.He also pointed to a shift in student politics. "What I find most interesting is that AISA and NSUI are fighting together today. This wasn't the case in the past," he said.As CJP leaders' arrests drew support across party lines, this cooperation was no longer limited to student organisations.The support for CJP has not come from Congress alone.TMC leader Mamata Banerjee condemned the arrests as an attempt to intimidate young protesters. Party MP Abhishek Banerjee accused the BJP of arresting people for waving the national flag, calling it "BJP's new Pakistanified Bharat". Mahua Moitra also expressed solidarity.AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal questioned whether waving the Tricolour could be a crime. DMK president MK Stalin offered legal assistance to the two CJP leaders, while NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Aaditya Thackeray condemned the arrests.The Left maintained its support. Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan criticised the arrests. CPI general secretary D Raja called the police action undemocratic and said his party's student and youth organisations would intensify their campaign for the right to protest at Jantar Mantar.The growing opposition presence was visible beyond Delhi. On Thursday, Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which had stayed away from earlier anti-CEC demonstrations, joined a Congress-led INDIA bloc protest in Chennai. TVK had joined the alliance on October 3; leaders from VCK, MDMK and other partners also participated.More protests may follow. NCP(SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande said Rahul had asked INDIA bloc leaders to be prepared for further demonstrations at 24 hours' notice.These parties have their own priorities and have not always followed the same protest programme. Yet, from Delhi to Chennai, more opposition leaders are speaking out on the same issue. CJP and the INDIA bloc, however, have not announced any joint protest programme.The BJP has rejected the opposition's allegations, accusing rivals of using street demonstrations to question democratic institutions after electoral defeats.On October 10, BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad said: "We are not opposed to protests, but you have weaponised street protests because of your electoral defeats."BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra also questioned whether events at Jantar Mantar represented the larger picture of India. The Election Commission has denied allegations of political bias in electoral-roll revision.For CJP, opposition support presents an opportunity and a challenge. The group has built its identity as an independent youth-led movement, but the detention of its leaders and criticism of its leadership raise questions about sustaining the agitation without established parties.Uday Chandra cautioned against reading too much into the cooperation."There is certainly a convergence of interests at this moment, but we should not mistake that for anything akin to a formal alliance. The police crackdown and detention of protesters have created a common cause for the CJP and the INDIA bloc," Chandra said.He noted that CJP's independence has been central to its youth appeal and that its leaders have criticised the opposition in the past.Political commentator Sugata Srinivasaraju questioned whether CJP had established a support base strong enough to sustain a larger movement. He warned that becoming an extension of Congress could cost it its independent identity. Nor was it clear whether CJP would lead any joint campaign or give way to a larger party.For Congress, CJP's ability to mobilise young people is attractive. But could closer cooperation undermine the independence that made those movements appealing in the first place?Chandra warned: "The autonomy of these youth movements is precisely what makes them politically significant. If parties or their student unions undermine that autonomy, the movement may splinter amidst loud bickering, and can even fizzle out following discord."CJP founder Dipke has maintained that the group will remain an independent pressure group, despite sharing the opposition's demand for Kumar's removal.The INDIA bloc has struggled to present a united front since its inception. Disagreements over leadership, seat-sharing and political priorities have divided parties, and Congress has faced criticism over its lack of efforts to keep the coalition together.The protests against the CEC have offered a different picture: common ground emerging from demonstrations rather than electoral negotiations. Differences remain, however. AAP and DMK, once part of the INDIA bloc, are still not ready to join hands with Congress.But does a greater presence on the streets mean the opposition has finally found its feet?Sugata Srinivasaraju disagreed that the opposition had been missing in action. Parties, he argued, had always been active, even if street demonstrations had recently become more frequent."More frequent protests do not necessarily mean a more effective opposition. Without planning, structure and a clear strategy, such demonstrations can become counterproductive, with little lasting political impact," he said.He also questioned what the prominence of youth leaders from outside Congress said about its leadership."It also reflects the opposition's inability to lead itself and absence of strong, charismatic leaders of its own. By bringing in faces from youth-led movements, it is, in a way, acknowledging that leadership gap. But there is a risk that leaders like Neha Bora could lose their independent identity within a larger political organisation, much like what happened with Kanhaiya Kumar," he said.The coming together of opposition parties has changed the picture on the streets, but questions remain over whether they can sustain protests, develop new leaders and turn a common cause into a coordinated campaign.For years, the question has been: Where is the opposition? With parties now finding common ground after months of differences, could that question finally have an answer?
Article Summary: Congress and CJP appeared to be competing for space and prominence while leading separate campaigns against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The trigger for greater unity came after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested on October 14 following their attempt to protest at Jantar Mantar.

The EAM hosted the SCO FMs meeting Goa; the FM of Botswana in Kevadia; Heart of Asia conference in Amritsar," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.He further said Rubio's visit would provide an opportunity for both sides to review India-US relations and discuss ways to further strengthen Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.Discussions are expected to cover key areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade and investment, defence, critical and emerging technologies, and other areas of mutual interest."The two sides will also exchange views on regional and global developments. The visit will provide an opportunity to sustain the high-level engagement between the two countries and advance our shared priorities," said Jaiswal.After his "productive" meeting with the UAE minister Thursday, Jaishankar will have another meeting with Al Nahyan Monday. Jaishankar visited UAE this week. The ministers will review bilateral cooperation under India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. "The delegations will assess and take forward initiatives in the areas of energy, trade and investments, fintech, defence and connectivity," said the official.The ministers discussed West Asia and the Strait of Hormuz situation. "Exchanged perspectives on bilateral and global issues in the spirit of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," said Jaishankar in a post on X.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar will host US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Oct 20. Jaishankaar will also host UAE counterp-art Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan a day earlier. The ministers will review bilateral cooperation under India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

Article Title: Two vessels carrying 24 Indian seafarers hit by projectiles, drone in separate incidents; all safe
Article Text:
Indian seafarers safe after tanker hit in Strait of Hormuz and another off Romania (representative image)

India has raised concerns over attacks on commercial vessels

NEW DELHI: Two vessels carrying a total of 24 Indian seafarers were struck in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and off Romania, Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said on Friday, adding that all crew members were safe and no casualties or injuries had been reported.In a post on X on Friday night, Sonowal said crude oil tanker MT ST 3, carrying 15 Indian seafarers, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 16. In a separate incident on October 14, chemical tanker YARA J, carrying nine Indian seafarers, was hit by a drone at Sulina Anchorage, Romania.“Thankfully, all 24 Indian nationals across both vessels are completely safe with no casualties or injuries,” the minister said.He added that the government was monitoring both situations and remaining in close contact with the ship management companies to ensure the security and well-being of the crew members.The latest incidents come amid repeated attacks on commercial shipping involving Indian seafarers in the Middle East and the Black Sea region.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) had earlier condemned attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on October 11, describing the recurring incidents as deeply concerning and warning that they risked aggravating an already volatile situation.The ministry said tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, had reportedly been struck by a drone at Sohar Anchorage. Nine crew members were rescued, while two remained missing.Another vessel, MT VALTHERA, a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker, was struck by an unidentified projectile, causing a fire on board. All 11 Indian seafarers on the vessel were reported safe, the MEA said.The ministry reiterated that the safety and security of Indian seafarers remained a priority for the government and called for immediate de-escalation and a resolution to the conflict between the United States and Iran through dialogue and diplomacy.It also called for an end to attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure, stressing the need to uphold freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded movement of maritime commerce through international waterways in accordance with international law.India has also raised concerns over attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. In a separate development the previous week, the MEA condemned further strikes on commercial vessels and called for an immediate cessation of violence in the interest of peace and stability.The ministry had also referred to external affairs minister S Jaishankar’s remarks that India remained in contact with Russia and Ukraine over its proposal for safe shipping in the Black Sea and “non-attack possibilities”, while addressing concerns raised by both sides over grain and energy exports.
Article Summary: Two vessels carrying a total of 24 Indian seafarers were struck in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and off Romania. Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all crew members were safe and no casualties or injuries had been reported. Latest incidents come amid repeated attacks on commercial shipping involving Indian seafarer in the Middle East and Black Sea region.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined an urgent hearing on a plea challenging the New Delhi Municipal Council's decision to shut Central Park in Connaught Place ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's ( CJP ) proposed ‘Lehra do Tiranga’ protest, saying it hoped “better sense will prevail” among all concerned.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it was conscious of the difficulties that a closure could cause to small shopkeepers and their families, while observing that the right to protest, the need to maintain law and order and the livelihood of traders were interconnected issues.“We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship and difficulty entire families will face,” the bench said.Justice Bagchi said the court could intervene if the restrictions resulted in business losses, adding that it would consider exercising its constitutional jurisdiction if required."If there's loss of business, we will exercise our powers under Constitutional jurisdiction. Let's cross that bridge when it comes," Justice Bagchi said.During the hearing, the petitioner's lawyer submitted that the NDMC had issued directions late Thursday night to close Central Park, effectively preventing businesses from operating in the area. The civic body had announced that the park would remain closed to the public on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons.The bench indicated that the plea could be listed on October 26 or 27.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has called on citizens to gather at Central Park with the national flag at 5 pm on Friday, alleging that party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were jailed for unfurling the Tricolour. The party has said it will proceed with the march despite the closure of the park and security restrictions.In a post on X, Dipke defended the party's protests, rejected allegations that it was promoting anarchy and accused the government of restricting democratic rights."Businesses do not suffer because of peaceful protests. They suffer when the govt decides to shut down an entire city, suspend internet services and restrict the movement of its own citizens and turn the city into a war-zone.""Since its inception, the Cockroach Janta Party has maintained that we will always follow Mahatma Gandhi’s path of peace and non-violence, and we have stood by that commitment. We have organised protests in Mumbai, Pune, Jaipur, Lucknow, Bengaluru and Nagpur, and every single one of them has been peaceful. I was personally assaulted in Jaipur, but even then, I chose not to retaliate because responding to violence with violence goes against everything we believe in. We would rather exercise the rights guaranteed to us by the Constitution, drafted under the leadership of Dr. BR Ambedkar, than resort to physical force. Our strength comes from our commitment to constitutional values, and no amount of provocation will make us abandon them.""Despite this, there are constant attempts to portray us as anarchists simply because we refuse to remain silent. But demanding answers from the govt is not anarchy, protesting against injustice on the streets is not anarchy, and questioning those who hold public office is certainly not anarchy. These are the most fundamental expressions of democracy. The very party that is in power today spent decades organising protests, taking to the streets and questioning the governments of the day when it was in opposition. Had the same restrictions, intimidation and police crackdowns been used against them, many of those who occupy positions of power today might never have reached where they are. It is deeply hypocritical to celebrate protests as a democratic right when you are in opposition and treat the same act as a threat to public order when you come to power."ALSO READ: ‘No one called Mahatma Gandhi African’: Sanjay Raut slams order against actor Imran Khan "We are not asking for privileges or special treatment. We are simply asking to exercise the rights that belong to every citizen of this Republic, irrespective of which party is in power. So let us fulfil our duty as citizens of this country by questioning those we elect, demanding accountability and speaking up whenever we witness injustice.""A govt that has been elected by the people is bound to listen to the people, not silence them. Democracy does not end once the votes have been counted."The proposed demonstration comes amid a standoff between the CJP and Delhi Police over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The CJP had announced the march after Das and Ranka were arrested for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, and raising slogans demanding Kumar's resignation. They were subsequently remanded to five days of judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail.Dipke has urged political parties and civil society organisations to set aside ideological differences and join the demonstration."I request all political parties and civil society groups to rise above ideology and come together. If the right to vote is not saved, democracy will not be saved," Dipke said at a press conference on Thursday.He also questioned the scale of voter deletions during the SIR exercise and alleged that the revisions could affect electoral outcomes."The margin of victory in 2024 was just 2 per cent. Over 13 crore voters deleted -- around 14 percent," he said."Where 2 per cent is deciding the election, you are deleting 13 crore votes. What is this if not a setting?" he added.The CJP has alleged that the government is shielding Kumar from scrutiny. These allegations have not been established by the court.Delhi Police has said Connaught Place is not a designated site for protests and that demonstrations can be held at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permissions."Jantar Mantar has been denotified as a designated protest site. Protesters can hold demonstrations at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permission," a senior police officer said.Security has been tightened around Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar, with several companies of paramilitary personnel stationed in the national capital. Police are deploying personnel at strategic locations, erecting barricades and regulating the movement of protesters and commuters to prevent any untoward incident.The NDMC issued its closure notice on Thursday, stating that Central Park would remain shut on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons. The decision came a day after the CJP announced its proposed march at the park, located in the centre of Connaught Place's inner circle.The party's agitation began in Mumbai on October 2 and subsequently moved to Delhi. On October 10, a planned demonstration at Jantar Mantar was met with a police crackdown, with Dipke, Das and Ranka detained at the airport after arriving from Mumbai. Opposition leaders, activists and students were also detained during protests in the capital.On October 13, CJP members entered the barricaded Jantar Mantar site carrying the national flag and were detained.Opposition parties and student organisations have separately held demonstrations against the SIR exercise and demanded accountability from the Election Commission. INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission headquarters on October 6 and were stopped by police barricades. Opposition leaders later met President Droupadi Murmu on October 9 to raise their concerns.The CJP has since framed its proposed Connaught Place march as a campaign for voting rights and the constitutional right to protest, setting up another confrontation over the restrictions imposed on demonstrations in central Delhi.
Article Summary: Supreme Court declines urgent plea against Central Park closure ahead of ’s Tiranga march. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has called on citizens to gather at Central Park with the national flag at 5 pm on Friday. The party has said it will proceed with the march despite the closure of the park.

Article Title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
Article Text:
Mittal launched her party, the Jan Neeti Bharat Party.

2. Ajit Jogi

3. Mani Shankar Aiyar

4. Arvind Kejriwal

5. KJ Alphons

NEW DELHI: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Thursday launched the Jan Neeti Bharat party and announced that it would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career to pursue politics independently.In a video message on X, Mittal said the party will focus on making people central to policymaking and ensuring that the government remains accountable to them throughout its five-year term, rather than only on election day."Politics rules over you. In Jan Neeti, you will be the ones who rule," she said, announcing the party's name and its decision to contest the state polls due early next year.Her decision to launch a party of her own places her among a group of civil servants who left government service before their scheduled retirement to enter politics.Here are 10 former civil servants who made the transition from bureaucracy to politics before completing their service.Yashwant Sinha resigned from the Indian Administrative Service in 1984 to enter active politics. He joined the Janata Party and subsequently became associated with the Janata Dal before joining the BJP.Sinha first served as Union finance minister in the Chandra Shekhar government in 1990-91.Under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, he returned to the finance ministry in 1998 and held the portfolio until 2002, when he became external affairs minister.His political career also included membership of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Sinha later distanced himself from the BJP and joined the Trinamool Congress in 2021, before contesting the 2022 presidential election as the opposition's joint candidate.Ajit Jogi left the IAS in 1986 to enter politics and joined the Congress. He had served as a district collector before moving into political life and was subsequently elected to the Rajya Sabha.Jogi's biggest political breakthrough came in 2000, when Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh. He became the newly created state's first chief minister, holding office until 2003.After years in the Congress, Jogi broke away from the party in 2016 and founded the Janata Congress Chhattisgarh, seeking to establish an independent regional political platform.His career stands out as an example of a former administrator moving from district-level governance to the leadership of a newly formed state and later attempting to build a party of his own.Mani Shankar Aiyar resigned from the Indian Foreign Service in 1989 to enter politics. He had served as a diplomat for more than two decades and spent part of his career on deputation to the Prime Minister's Office under Rajiv Gandhi.Aiyar joined the Congress and won the Mayiladuthurai Lok Sabha seat in Tamil Nadu in 1991. He went on to become a prominent party leader and served as Union minister for petroleum and natural gas during the UPA government.He also held the panchayati raj portfolio and was involved in efforts to strengthen local self-government institutions.Arvind Kejriwal resigned from the Indian Revenue Service in 2006 after working in the income tax department. He had become involved in the Right to Information movement and founded the non-governmental organisation Parivartan to address citizens' grievances.His political journey gathered momentum during the Ana Hazare-led India Against Corruption movement, which campaigned for a stronger anti-corruption law. In 2012, Kejriwal founded the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), choosing to build a political organisation rather than join an established party.AAP made its electoral debut in the 2013 Delhi assembly elections, when Kejriwal defeated then chief minister Sheila Dikshit. He became Delhi chief minister in December 2013 and returned to the post after the party's victories in 2015 and 2020.KJ Alphons took voluntary retirement from the IAS in 2006 and entered electoral politics in Kerala. He contested the Kanjirappally assembly seat in Kerala as an independent candidate supported by the Left Democratic Front and won.Alphons later founded the Jana Shakti platform before joining the BJP in 2011. His political journey subsequently took him to Parliament, when he became a Rajya Sabha member.In 2017, he was inducted into the Narendra Modi government as Union minister of state for tourism, with independent charge, and also handled electronics and information technology.His transition from a civil servant known for urban development initiatives to a state-level politician and Union minister is an example of an officer moving across political formations during his career.Satyapal Singh, a 1980-batch IPS officer of the Maharashtra cadre, opted for voluntary retirement in January 2014 while serving as Mumbai police commissioner, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.He joined the BJP and contested the Baghpat Lok Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh in 2014, defeating Rashtriya Lok Dal chief Ajit Singh. He retained the constituency in the 2019 general election.Singh served as Union minister of state for human resource development and water resources during the Modi government's first term. Before entering politics, he had served in several police leadership roles and was known for his work in law enforcement.OP Choudhary, a 2005-batch IAS officer, resigned from the service in 2018 while serving as Raipur collector to enter politics. He joined the BJP and contested the Kharsia assembly constituency in Chhattisgarh in the same year.Choudhary lost that election but returned to the electoral contest in 2023, this time winning the Raipur City South seat. He was subsequently inducted into the Chhattisgarh government as a minister.His career highlights the uncertain transition from administration to politics. Unlike officers who win their first election, Choudhary's initial defeat did not end his political ambitions. He returned five years later and secured a place in the state Cabinet.Aparajita Sarangi, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Odisha cadre, took voluntary retirement in 2018 while serving as joint secretary in the Union rural development ministry.She joined the BJP in November that year and contested the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Bhubaneswar. Sarangi won the seat, defeating Biju Janata Dal candidate Arup Patnaik.She retained the constituency in the 2024 general election, establishing herself as a BJP leader in Odisha.Sarangi's transition was particularly swift: she moved from a senior central government position to an electoral contest within months of leaving the service and subsequently secured two consecutive Lok Sabha victories.AK Sharma, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre, took voluntary retirement in January 2021, around 18 months before his scheduled superannuation.Sharma had spent a substantial part of his career working in the Prime Minister's Office and was associated with Narendra Modi's administration during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister and later as prime minister.After leaving the service, Sharma joined the BJP and was elected to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council. He subsequently became a minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, handling portfolios including urban development and energy.His move demonstrated how a senior bureaucrat with experience in the central administration could enter state politics and secure a position in the Cabinet without first contesting a direct assembly election.Asim Arun, a 1994-batch IPS officer, took voluntary retirement in January 2022 while serving as Kanpur police commissioner. He joined the BJP soon afterwards, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Arun contested the Kannauj assembly seat and won, entering a constituency associated with the Samajwadi Party. He was subsequently inducted into the Yogi Adityanath government.His political entry came within weeks of his voluntary retirement, making him one of the clearest recent examples of a serving police officer moving directly into electoral politics before the end of his career.K Annamalai, a 2011-batch IPS officer of the Karnataka cadre, resigned from the police service in September 2019, before completing his tenure. He had served as superintendent of police in Udupi and Chikkamagaluru districts before leaving the force.He joined the BJP in August 2020 and rose rapidly through the party's ranks. In July 2021, he was appointed the BJP's Tamil Nadu president, becoming one of the party's most prominent faces in the state.Annamalai contested the 2021 Tamil Nadu assembly election from Aravakurichi but lost to the DMK's R Elango. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, he contested from Coimbatore but lost to DMK candidate Ganapathi P Rajkumar.In June 2026, Annamalai quit the BJP following differences with the party leadership over its political strategy in Tamil Nadu and launched a new political movement, 'We The Leaders'. He said the movement would focus on "common man politics", challenge what he described as "cult and dynastic politics", and eventually evolve into a political party. He has outlined plans to contest the 2031 Tamil Nadu assembly elections.
Article Summary: Divya Mittal launched her party, the Jan Neeti Bharat Party, on Thursday. The party will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career.

Abuse of authority and workplace humiliation must be addressed with utmost seriousness,” the women's rights body added.The NCW’s action came after a video purportedly showed senior IAS officer Kumar Rajeev Ranjan, administrative secretary of Jammu and Kashmir’s Department of Labour and Employment, allegedly abusing a junior female officer during a video conference meeting, calling her “bloody sh*t”.In the purported video, Ranjan can be seen questioning Beenish Wani, a Jammu and Kashmir Administrative Service (JKAS) officer posted as Assistant Director, Employment, in Ganderbal, over her performance.Wani told him that she had written to the deputy commissioner and additional deputy commissioner after the district officer of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) said targets could not be achieved and that officials would not cooperate. Ranjan asked her to obtain the response in writing and says she should have informed him directly about the matter.“Why do you need NRLM if others are doing the work? Do you only have to write letters and seek the medal? They are just a helping tool, not the main authority,” Ranjan is heard saying in the video.Wani replied that NRLM is needed to assist them, but Ranjan tells her to “shut up”.When she asked Ranjan to let her explain and questions why he was shouting, the IAS officer responded, “You are bloody sh*t. I can always talk to you like this.”When Wani objected, Ranjan told her to “get out” and asked for an order suspending her to be issued.She later told reporters that the incident took place during a review meeting on Wednesday and that she had raised the matter with higher authorities.
Article Summary: The National Commission for Women (NCW) has taken suo motu cognisance of a viral video purportedly showing a senior Jammu and Kashmir IAS officer verbally abusing a junior female officer. The NCW has sought an action taken report (ATR) within seven days.

Article Title: India diversified crude oil sources from 27 to 41 amid disruptions in Hormuz, Red Sea: Hardeep Puri

NEW DELHI: India has expanded its crude oil supply network from 27 countries to 41 and will continue to diversify imports, increase refining capacity and explore new sources of oil amid geopolitical tensions, minister for petroleum and natural gas Hardeep Singh Puri said.“We have diversified our sources of supply from 27 to 41,” he said, while speaking at the Pathways to Viksit Bharat Conclave at Shri Ram College of Commerce, ANI reported.Puri said disruptions to international shipping routes could have a direct impact on Indian industries and household expenses.“A disruption along a distant shipping route can alter the costs of an Indian factory and the budget of an Indian household,” Puri said.Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the event, Puri said India was importing more than 5 million barrels of oil per day while exporting around 1 million barrels, supported by its expanding refining capacity.He said India’s crude oil procurement would continue to be guided by the availability of supplies at competitive prices. He also pointed to emerging tensions in the Red Sea, saying the government was monitoring the situation and working to ensure uninterrupted supplies.The minister said India would also need to raise domestic energy production to meet growing demand as economic expansion and industrial activity drive up consumption.He expressed confidence that the Samudra Manthan scheme, which supports deep-sea oil and gas exploration, would help strengthen domestic output over the next three years. ANI reported.Under the scheme, the government plans to provide resources for drilling 150 wells, Puri said, stressing the need for investment in exploration to unlock the country’s domestic oil and gas potential.

NEW DELHI: India on Friday strongly rejected US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal 's remarks concerning the country's electoral process, calling them “unwarranted and uninformed” and accusing her of interfering in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy.Responding to a question during a bi-weekly media briefing in New Delhi, ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the remarks undermined democratic principles.“We find the remarks of the Congresswoman unwarranted and uninformed and tantamount to interfering in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy. This is an approach that undermines democracy itself,” Jaiswal said.The response followed Jayapal's expression of concern over reports of names being removed from India's electoral rolls.The Democrat representing Washington state wrote on X, “I am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls.”India's Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, had also dismissed Jayapal's allegations on Thursday, describing them as interference in India's internal affairs.“The remarks by Rep. NEW DELHI: Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar on Saturday accused the Centre of acting arbitrarily over the proposed delimitation exercise, questioning why the government was reluctant to convene an all-party meeting on the issue.His remarks came a day after Congress president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the fourth time, demanding an all-party meeting to discuss the delimitation proposals before they are finalised and introduced in Parliament.“Modi Govt is acting arbitrarily. They did not even get the majority; they formed the Govt with support of other parties. Opposition is strong. But irrespective of the Opposition being strong or small, such matters should be discussed by both sides...Why is the Govt scared? Because they have done wrong. So, they won't convene (an all-party meeting) and discuss...” Wadettiwar said.He stressed that matters of national importance should be discussed with both the ruling alliance and the Opposition, irrespective of the latter's strength.In his letter to Modi on Friday, Kharge raised procedural and constitutional concerns over the status of Parliament's Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but had not been formally prorogued.“It has already been 64 days since the Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13, 2026 and both Houses of Parliament are yet to be prorogued. This scenario is unprecedented,” Kharge wrote.Adjournment sine die suspends parliamentary proceedings indefinitely without specifying a date for the next sitting. Prorogation, by contrast, formally ends a session through an order issued by the President of India.Kharge argued that the prolonged delay in proroguing both Houses had fuelled speculation about a possible sudden reconvening of Parliament or an extension of the session, potentially bypassing the standard notice periods for lawmakers.Kharge urged the Centre to clarify the status of the Monsoon Session and convene an all-party meeting before introducing any new delimitation proposals.The Congress has also called for political parties and regional stakeholders to be given sufficient time to examine draft legislation before it is brought to Parliament.That shift from constitutional mandate to parliamentary choice was the provision that most alarmed critics.

Article Title: 'Verify before she vilifies': India rejects UN rapporteur's claims on youth protests
