NEW DELHI: India has rejected allegations by UN special rapporteur Gina Romero that young people in the country face retaliation and stigmatisation for discussing mental health and gender justice, calling the claims based on anonymous and unverified submissions.Speaking at an interactive dialogue with Romero during the 81st session of the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee, India’s first secretary Anuj Swarup questioned the evidence cited in her report on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and association.“Yet, the special rapporteur, Ms Gina Romero, asserts that young people in India face retaliation or stigmatisation for discussing mental health or gender justice, though merely citing unnamed submissions in the footnote. This level of arbitrary report writing is precisely the reason that the United Nations and its institutions have lost credibility,” Swarup said.“A sweeping charge against the world's largest youth population resting on anonymous and unverified claims is not evidence. It is hearsay, dressed up as a UN report, and my delegation rejects it outright,” he added.Swarup said India’s Constitution guarantees freedom of assembly, association, speech and expression under Article 19, with these rights protected by an independent judiciary, a free press and the National Human Rights Commission.He also cited young people’s participation in political movements and engagement with senior government leaders as evidence of civic space in the country.“In which repressive state does a satirical youth party question the government, marches on the capital, and then sits across the table with senior national leaders?” he asked, referring to a youth-led political movement mentioned in Romero’s report.“Chair, a mandate holder who relies on anonymous inputs to generalise for 1.4 billion people does a disservice to the very mandate she holds. We urge this special rapporteur to verify before she vilifies and to bring the required rigour and fairness in her reports,” he said.The remarks come amid heightened scrutiny of the government’s handling of youth protests, including demonstrations over alleged irregularities in public examinations and the recent anti-SIR stir.Romero had alleged in posts on X on October 10 that peaceful youth protesters in India faced excessive force and arbitrary detention. She also claimed that more than 2,500 protesters had been sent to remote detention centres without legal support, with some allegedly tortured or sexually assaulted. She further alleged that phones had been seized, protest-related material deleted and internet access restricted.These allegations were made by Romero and were not independently established in the information provided by India’s statement.India, meanwhile, defended its response to student protests over examination irregularities, saying the government had engaged with young people and taken steps to address exam fraud.Swarup said Parliament had amended the Public Examinations Act, doubled punishments for paper leaks, overhauled the examination system and created fast-track courts in every state to prosecute exam fraud.He also pointed to the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue, saying more than five million young people had participated this year and helped shape national priorities through direct engagement with the Prime Minister.
Article Summary: India rejects UN rapporteur Gina Romero’s claims on youth protests in the country. India calls the claims based on anonymous and unverified submissions. Romero had alleged that peaceful youth protesters in India faced excessive force and arbitrary detention. She also claimed that more than 2,500 protesters had been sent to remote detention centres without legal support.

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader and former Union minister P Chidambaram on Saturday defended the use of the phrase “regime change” in a democracy, amid a political row over remarks by student activist Neha Bora and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan during protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In a post on X, Chidambaram questioned the BJP's reaction to the phrase and said the Opposition's duty was to “oppose, expose and depose” the government.“Why is the BJP apoplectic with feigned rage on the use of the phrase 'regime change'? The Congress has maintained that peaceful protests against an elected government and efforts to replace it through elections are legitimate democratic activities.The BJP, however, has argued that references to Bangladesh and the language used by some protest organisers point to a broader attempt to create political unrest.Several BJP leaders criticised the opposition over the remarks, including Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, party president Nitin Nabin, Uttar Pradesh BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary, Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi, Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. Article Title: PM Modi to visit Canada on December 11-12, Mark Carney confirms after phone call

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11-12, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said, as New Delhi and Ottawa seek to strengthen bilateral ties and advance cooperation in trade, energy, technology and security.Carney confirmed the dates while speaking to visitors at a restaurant in Calgary on Thursday, saying he had “just spoke” to PM Modi about the upcoming visit. He said the PM Modi would travel to Toronto and Ottawa, adding, “We’ll see if we can broaden it out.”The Indian High Commission in Ottawa subsequently confirmed the December 11-12 visit in a post on X, saying the two leaders had agreed to build on the positive momentum in bilateral relations and work towards concrete outcomes across key sectors.The confirmation came amid renewed diplomatic engagement between the two countries, with both sides pushing to expand economic cooperation and conclude negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).However, the ministry of external affairs had said on Friday that the dates were still under discussion.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: “As you are aware, foreign minister of Canada visited India a few days back.She met with the external affairs minister (S Jaishankar) and discussed progress in bilateral ties. She also called on the Prime Minister. During the visit, the PM Modi's visit to Canada came up for discussion. The dates for the visit are presently under discussion. We will announce the visit at the appropriate time. ”PM Modi's proposed visit comes as the two countries seek to conclude negotiations on CEPA by the end of 2026, with the agreement expected to support efforts to double bilateral trade by 2030.Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand discussed the trade pact and ways to expand cooperation during her meeting with Modi in New Delhi earlier this week. The discussions covered trade, investment, energy, education, culture, technology and security.According to a readout issued by the Canadian government, the two leaders also discussed the Team Canada Trade Mission to India, led by Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu, as an effort to expand bilateral trade and strengthen Canada's engagement in the Indo-Pacific.“Minister Anand and PM Modi discussed the importance of concluding a comprehensive economic partnership agreement by the end of the year and highlighted the Team Canada Trade Mission led by International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu as a tangible example of growing the economic partnership, expansion of bilateral trade and advancing Canada's broader engagements in the Indo-Pacific,” the statement read.Following the meeting, Modi described the discussions as productive and reiterated India's commitment to strengthening ties with Canada.“Pleased to meet Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand. We had a productive discussion on further strengthening India-Canada ties in trade, technology, security, energy, education and people-to-people exchanges,” PM Modi said in a post on X.“India is committed to building a constructive and forward-looking strategic partnership with Canada that delivers tangible benefits to the people of both countries,” he added.Anand also expressed optimism about the relationship, saying the two countries had considerable scope to expand cooperation in trade, investment and security.“Canada and India have enormous potential to shape a more prosperous future, together. I had the opportunity to meet with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi today to discuss our strategic partnership and the opportunities ahead for trade, investment and security,” she said.“From Prime Minister Carney's visit earlier this year to the Team Canada Trade Mission underway, our renewed engagement reflects a growing ambition to turn shared priorities into lasting opportunities for both nations,” Anand said, adding that Canada looked forward to welcoming PM Modi in December.The planned visit follows a telephone conversation between PM Modi and Carney earlier this week, during which the two leaders discussed strengthening the India-Canada strategic partnership.PM Modi described the conversation as warm and productive, stressing the importance of closer cooperation between the two countries.“Together, India and Canada are contributing towards a more stable and prosperous world,” PM Modi said in a post on X.According to the Canadian Prime Minister's Office, the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to concluding CEPA negotiations at the earliest opportunity and advancing efforts to double bilateral trade by 2030.Anand's visit also included discussions on the progress made under the India-Canada joint roadmap. The two sides welcomed a bilateral security dialogue held in India the previous week as part of continued engagement on security and law enforcement at the national security adviser level.The renewed diplomatic engagement comes as India and Canada seek to translate improved political ties into tangible cooperation across economic and strategic sectors.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11-12, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said. Announcement comes amid renewed diplomatic engagement between the two countries. Both sides pushing to expand economic cooperation and conclude negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)

Article Title: 'Women ought to be released after sunset': Neha Bora questions night-long detentions over anti-SIR stir

NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora on Saturday questioned the overnight detention of protesters, over the anti-SIR stir, saying women ought to be released after sunset and alleging that police denied her access to a lawyer for hours.Bora was detained under preventive provisions on the evening of October 16 and released early Saturday after formal procedures under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act, Delhi Police said.“Under what authority is this justified? By what law or order is it permissible to keep detainees held in custody all night long? Legally, individuals, especially women, ought to be released after sunset, yet this is not happening,” Bora said.She alleged that police demanded her personal details but did not allow her to speak to or consult a lawyer for a long time. “Our lawyers spent 5–6 hours trying to reach me. What kind of chaos and anarchy? The one you unleashed in Central Delhi? The people of Delhi cannot even breathe a sigh of relief; whichever route they take to get to work, they find it blocked. You are spreading chaos and anarchy across the nation. Please, spare the people of India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR, so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," she added.Calling for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s impeachment and a halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, she said the move was necessary to ensure citizens’ voting rights.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, who was also detained on Friday evening ahead of the ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest, is set to be produced before a special executive magistrate court.Delhi Police said action under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita was initiated against him.CJP had earlier alleged that Dipke was taken to an undisclosed location and denied access to lawyers, claiming his family and party members were unable to contact him for more than 10 hours. NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Saturday said that Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora were detained under preventive provisions on the evening of October 16.While Bora was subsequently released early Saturday, Dipke is set to be produced before a special executive magistrate (SEM) court.According to Delhi Police, Bora was released after formal procedures under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act, while action under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was initiated against Dipke.Police sources told news agency PTI that Dipke was detained from Jhandewalan while he was on his way to Connaught Place to attend the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' protest on Friday evening.Meanwhile, CJP had alleged that Dipke was "kidnapped" by the police, claiming that his family, lawyers and party members had been unable to establish contact with him for more than 10 hours after his detention.In a post on X, the party said it had received no information about his whereabouts since he was picked up ahead of the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' protest."The Delhi Police has taken Abhijeet Dipke to an undisclosed location.We have lost contact with him. Mahalaya Amavasya has just passed, ending a sacred period of remembrance for our ancestors . As the anticipation of Navarathri fills the air, we move from honouring those who came before us to celebrating the divine feminine. Yet, between these observances lies a profound connection: our lives are rooted in the past, even as we journey towards the future.Across civilizations, humanity has found ways to honour the departed. In Chinese shrines, three incense sticks are offered, symbolising ancestors, the present generation and future descendants. In Mexico,, the Day of the Dead, celebrates the departed with food and flowers. In Japan,is observed with the belief that ancestral spirits return to visit their families. Rituals differ, but the sentiment remains universal: love does not end with death.In Hindu tradition , performing ancestral rites is regarded not simply as a choice, but as a sacred duty.Water occupies a place of profound significance in these rituals. Water is more than a natural element. It purifies, heals and connects the physical with the spiritual. Offering water to ancestors expresses gratitude and invokes their peace. Even in grief, flowing river offers comfort through its symbolism of transition, surrender and liberation. Fire purifies the physical; water, in its sacred symbolism, becomes a medium of spiritual release.An intriguing historical anecdote brings this tradition into focus. After Aurangzeb confined his father, Shah Jahan, in the Agra Fort in 1658, the ageing emperor lived under strict restrictions. Shah Jahan reproached his son for denying him adequate water, observing the irony that Hindus offered water and reverence even to departed ancestors, while his own son denied these to a living father. The poignancy of this remark endures: if reverence is owed to those beyond our sight, how much greater should our compassion be towards those still beside us?Thiruvalluvar, too, places ancestral obligations at the very beginning of the householder's duties. In43, he writes:The householder's foremost duties are towards the departed, the divine, guests, relatives and oneselfWhy does the poet place the departed before even the gods ? Perhaps he recognises that gratitude begins by acknowledging those whose lives and sacrifices have shaped our own.We do not know Valluvar 's religious identity. Yet his reference to ancestral duties suggests that honouring the departed was deeply embedded in the cultural life of his time.Across traditions, food, water and other offerings are made in memory of the dead, often through acts of charity. Perhaps what we offer to those we can see finds its way, through mysterious cosmic pathways, to those we cannot.An ancient prayer- Pithru Gayathri Manthra - expresses this enduring hope: Let us meditate upon the ancestors, the sustainers of the world; may they guide our consciousness.The departed may no longer walk beside us, but their footsteps remain on our paths. May their blessings dissolve our obstacles and strengthen our resolve.We are each a living chapter in a story written by generations before us, entrusted with the beautiful responsibility of being the link that carries their legacy into generations yet to come.
